svg.text: CUDA C programming, end to end — a concept map in factory terms
Each box gives the technical name, then the same idea as a worker, a crew, a bench or a truck in one giant plant. The head office (CPU) plans and phones orders across; the plant
(GPU) mass-produces. Read the bands top to bottom; follow the arrows to see what depends on what. State of play as of September 2026 (CUDA 13, Blackwell fleets, Rubin arriving).
1 · TWO BUILDINGS · why GPUs exist: latency vs throughput · 2006 →
2 · THE WORK ORDER · kernels: writing them, launching them
3 · THE WORKFORCE · threads, warps, blocks and grids
4 · THE FACTORY FLOOR · what the hardware does with your threads
5 · THE WAREHOUSE · the memory hierarchy, fastest to slowest
6 · TRUCKS AND SHELVING · moving data, and touching it well
7 · WHISTLES AND LOGBOOKS · synchronisation, atomics, cooperation patterns
8 · MANY CONVEYOR LINES · streams, events and whole-plant flow
9 · THE TOOL CRIB · compiler, libraries, profilers — and when not to GPU
